reused_checks.reason: The source, tests, helper inputs, compiler and recorded results match. Rule 9 permits reuse across stages. Independent review found no concrete gap that requires another run.

coverage: The public startup test completes Reset, scan setup, discovery, CCCD subscription and MIDI delivery.
The receive tests check fragments, invalid lengths, bounds, rejected headers and lifecycle resets.
The signaling tests check identifiers, fragmented commands, MTU rejection, bounded reply queues, reply priority and normal MIDI.
The reconnect tests restore sole-link credits after successful Disconnection Complete and saturate completed-packet counts.
The abort tests distinguish transport acceptance, command responses and actual disconnection. They retain handles and credits through failure.
The deadline tests execute the extracted production service. They check cutoff minus 1, exact cutoff, cutoff plus 1 and timer wrap.
The stop tests use the actual production service with simulated dependencies. They check refused Cancel and Scan Disable retries.
The stop tests check one accepted control, successful Status without completion, failed Status and Complete, and absent completion.
The stop tests check repeated stop, direct start, late connection, duplicate connection, wrong handles, successful disconnection and fresh startup.
The stop tests check pending Create, pending Scan Enable, prior Scan Disable, accepted automatic Cancel and unrelated failed connection events.
The stop tests retain the original cutoff and reject late Disconnect submissions for both connection event variants and timer wrap.
The realistic saved Cancel probe uses a full public startup sequence and correctly sized 19-byte and 31-byte event parameters.
public_test_review.fixture_limit: The older deadline fixture uses a short enhanced-event layout. The new public stop fixture and saved realistic Cancel probe use the complete layout. Both execute the repaired race path. This does not leave the required event variants untested.
